## Options schema and YAML keys (the deck file) {#sec-ch15-options}

### Summary

A snapy run is configured by one YAML file, the *deck*. Every module that has options reads its own block of the
deck and refuses any key it does not know. Where a module's options are plain scalars, their names, deck keys,
types, defaults, documentation and checks are declared once, in a table under `src/options/`, and a generator
writes the C++ members, the `report()` text, the deck reader, the Python bindings and the Python stub from that
table. The rule exists so that a default or a check has one home: the table. A reader of the code, of the Python
stub or of a run's option report sees the same value, because all three come from the same row.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Turns the deck into the option objects of every module, with one definition per option and a refusal
of every unknown key.

**Data.** In: one YAML file. Out: `MeshBlockOptions` holding the layout, hydro, scalar, integrator, output,
coordinate and boundary options; a `report()` text per module.

**Placement.** Once, before any block exists: `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` reads the deck, then `MeshBlockImpl`
runs the setup checks when it is built.

**Activation.** Always. Defaults come from the tables; an absent block leaves its module at its defaults.

**Guarantee / limits.** An unknown key under a checked block stops the run with the key's path; an out-of-range
value of a checked row stops it with the row's message. Keys the tables do not list are read by hand-written
readers and are checked by those readers, not by the generator.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section, @tbl-ch15-options-tests.
:::

This section has no equations and no local symbols. *Aliases.* Lane O and its item O4 (the generated option
tables) in commit messages.

### Derivation

None: the section describes a schema, not a discretisation. Three rules take the place of a derivation, and each is
a property of the generated code rather than of the physics.

1. *One row, one option.* A row of a table under `src/options/` declares an option's member name, its deck key,
   its type, its default, how it is read, its environment-variable override if any, whether it reaches Python,
   and its documentation: the column list at the head of `gen_options.py` ({{< code tools/gen_options.py >}}).
   From that row the generator emits the member with its default, the `report()` line, the reader statement,
   the pybind11 binding and the `.pyi` stub block. A default therefore cannot differ between the C++ object,
   its report and the Python stub, because none of them is written by hand.
2. *Every checked block refuses an unknown key.* A reader that calls `check_keys`
   ({{< code src/input/check_keys.cpp check_keys >}}) on a block compares every key of the block with the keys it
   reads, plus the keys another reader reads from the same block, and stops at the first key on neither list with
   the message `unknown key '<path>/<key>'. Valid keys: ...`. A table declares the keys its block hands to other
   readers under `extra_keys`; in `hydro.yaml` ({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}) these are
   `equation-of-state`[^rg-5a10d3c13a00], `reconstruct`[^rg-f5a21213da88] and `riemann-solver`[^rg-96a1118440b3], read by their own modules.
3. *A check runs where its table says.* A row's check belongs to one or more *check sets*: `read`, which runs
   inside the deck reader right after the row it follows, or a named set the table declares, emitted as a
   separate function the code calls where that set applies (the `checks` column of `gen_options.py`,
   {{< code tools/gen_options.py >}}). The output table's `domain` set, for example, needs the resolved global
   grid, so it runs once per output when the block is built, in `MeshBlockImpl::reset`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}), not when the deck is read; the set is declared in
   `output.yaml` ({{< code src/options/output.yaml >}}).

### Numerical method

**The tables at the pin.** Six families of tables sit under `src/options/`: `coord.yaml`
({{< code src/options/coord.yaml >}}; the `geometry`[^rg-3079dbd32736] block: type, bounds with their `_pi` aliases, cells, `nghost`[^rg-22717fd4f164],
`interp_order`[^rg-a1f3b7685ff3], the stretched-grid keys `x1rat`[^rg-c80d72cc7be3] and `x1f`), `hydro.yaml` ({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}};
the scalar rows of `dynamics`[^rg-1c007ea215c1]), `layout.yaml` ({{< code src/options/layout.yaml >}}; the `distribute` block),
`output.yaml` ({{< code src/options/output.yaml >}}; one entry of the `outputs`[^rg-42ad95cc5381] list), `internal_boundary.yaml`
({{< code src/options/internal_boundary.yaml >}}; `boundary-condition/internal`) and one `forcing_<module>.yaml`
per forcing module. CMake runs the generator over all of them at configure time and writes the `.inc` files into
`snap_options/` (the `gen_options` step of the top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}); a module
includes its reader and its members from there, as `OutputOptionsImpl` does
({{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl >}}). The Python stubs carry the generated block between
two marker comments (`hydro.pyi`, {{< code python/snapy/hydro.pyi >}}; `output.pyi`,
{{< code python/snapy/output.pyi >}}).

**The `dynamics` rows.** `hydro.yaml` ({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}) declares, with their defaults:
`verbose` (false), `disable-flux-x1`[^rg-5cf47e45a36b], `-x2`, `-x3` (false; each also zeroes the gravity component of its
direction, see below), `wb-wall-clamp`[^rg-e2c1522ec93e] (true), `conversion-order`[^rg-e7e0b398ca96] (2; the value 4 selects the fourth-order $x_1$[^rg-7f8e197294fa]
conversion of @sec-ch04), `anomaly` (false; the environment variable `SNAP_ANOMALY` overrides the deck and the row
is not bound to Python), `flux-covariance` (true), `x1-mass-covariance` (false; it needs at least three $x_1$ cells
per block), `perturbation-flux` (false), `precision` (`float64`; @sec-ch12) and `conserve-axial-momentum` (`off`,
else `transport` or `exact`, with the word aliases `false`/`no` for `off` and `true`/`on`/`yes` for `transport`;
any other word is refused with a message that names the three values).

**The reading order of a deck.** `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads the deck in a fixed order:

1. the layout (`distribute`), through `LayoutOptionsImpl::from_yaml`;
2. the run's base name, the deck's file name without its extension; output files are named from it;
3. the hydro options, then the scalar options, whose reconstruction defaults to the hydro's horizontal
   reconstruction when the deck gives none, then the integrator;
4. `verbose` and the execution keys: `integration/execution` is the key that selects how the integrator runs,
   `auto`, `eager` or `cuda-graph`, and any other word is refused;
   `execution-strict` is refused with `eager`, because an eager run is never refused; the member `execution`[^rg-3dca53244575] and
   its default `auto` are declared in `MeshBlockOptionsImpl`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.hpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::execution >}}), and @sec-ch11 gives what each value
   does;
5. the `outputs` list: entry $n$ of the list becomes output `out<n>`; the position, not a key, sets its file id,
   in `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}});
6. the coordinate (`geometry`) and the internal boundary;
7. the external boundaries: the `boundary-condition` block admits `external`[^rg-ea7e99c37c8d] and `internal`[^rg-32e65e1b6134], the `external`
   block admits `x1-inner`[^rg-0e5e2673a49c] ... `x3-outer`[^rg-d42c6e4726b6], each defaulting to `reflecting`; a dimension with one cell that lies
   below an active one keeps two empty slots, so the face index is the same for every deck; `periodic` marks
   the layout; the name with its side appended (`reflecting_inner`, ...) must be a registered boundary function,
   else the run stops. Which function does what is @sec-ch14.

The hydro reader, `HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}),
reads, in order, the equation of state, the vertical and horizontal reconstruction, the Riemann solver, the
implicit correction and the sedimentation options, then the `dynamics` rows through the generated reader, then the
`forcing`[^rg-f1deea8dad7e] block: it must be a map; the retired key `fric-heat` is refused with a message that says why; the twelve
forcing keys are checked; each forcing module reads its own block, and a `plume-forcing` block is read only with
the `plume-eos` equation of state. When a direction's flux is disabled, the gravity component of that direction is
set to zero after the gravity block is read.

**Reporting.** With `verbose: true` every module prints its `report()` text, the generated `* name = value` lines
under the table's title, as the deck is read, from `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::report`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.hpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::report >}}). The expected text of the defaults is pinned by
a test (below).

### Code

**How to use it.** A minimal deck names the geometry, the dynamics and the boundaries; everything else takes its
table default:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `type`[^rg-c82d9b68904e], `bounds`[^rg-809be4d3f9f0], `x1min`[^rg-10ab5bffdcb5], `x1max`[^rg-d79568ee973b], `x2min`[^rg-b115e17b940c], `x2max`[^rg-af2dc6224b7d], `x3min`[^rg-76518649f79f], `x3max`[^rg-1bbca3a08d89], `cells`[^rg-a1f4e77675c4], `nx1`[^rg-c6b56440ed70], `nx2`[^rg-e49c72c32257], `nx3`[^rg-d0681286875c], `vertical`[^rg-8fd6ffd55072], `horizontal`[^rg-ff5f79e61217], `const-gravity`[^rg-dee65088947a], `grav1`[^rg-bc3127656067], `x1-outer`[^rg-9f9cfab229ca], `x2-inner`[^rg-578811b43af6], `x2-outer`[^rg-0e6812dc53be], `integration`[^rg-f528a638e9c3], `cfl`[^rg-b703d495f357], `tlim`[^rg-c07a7b10dcd1].
```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 1000., x2min: 0., x2max: 1000., x3min: 0., x3max: 1.}
  cells: {nx1: 64, nx2: 64, nx3: 1, nghost: 2}
dynamics:
  equation-of-state: {type: ideal-gas}
  reconstruct: {vertical: {type: weno5}, horizontal: {type: weno5}}
  riemann-solver: {type: hllc}
  conversion-order: 2          # a hydro.yaml row; 2 is the default
forcing:
  const-gravity: {grav1: -9.8}
boundary-condition:
  external: {x1-inner: reflecting, x1-outer: reflecting, x2-inner: periodic, x2-outer: periodic}
integration:
  type: rk3
  cfl: 0.4
  tlim: 600.
  execution: auto              # the default; eager or cuda-graph are the other values
```

**What is refused, and why.**

- An unknown key under a checked block, with the key's path in the message (rule 2). The checked blocks the
  tests exercise are listed in the Tests layer.
- `integration/execution` outside `auto`, `eager`, `cuda-graph`, and `execution-strict: true` with
  `execution: eager`, in `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
  ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}): strict means "refuse what cannot
  be captured", and eager never captures.
- `forcing/fric-heat`: the $x_1$ face gravity work already carries the sedimentation channel of the mass flux, so
  the key would apply the precipitation potential-energy release twice; `HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
  ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) says so in its message.
- `dynamics/conserve-axial-momentum` outside its three values: the row's check in `hydro.yaml`
  ({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}).
- An output entry without `type`, or with both a slice and a sum on one axis, a slice outside the global grid,
  or slices out of order (@sec-ch15-output).
- A boundary name that is not registered, in `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
  ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

**The excerpt.** The execution keys are checked once, by the deck reader `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), so a bad value never reaches a
block:

```cpp
  if (config["integration"]) {
    auto intg = config["integration"];
    op->execution() = intg["execution"].as<std::string>(op->execution());
    op->execution_strict() =
        intg["execution-strict"].as<bool>(op->execution_strict());
  }
  TORCH_CHECK(op->execution() == "auto" || op->execution() == "eager" ||
                  op->execution() == "cuda-graph",
              "integration/execution must be auto, eager or cuda-graph, got '",
              op->execution(), "'");
  TORCH_CHECK(!(op->execution() == "eager" && op->execution_strict()),
              "integration/execution-strict needs execution: cuda-graph "
              "(eager is never refused)");
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Only the tables' rows are generated. The sub-module options (equation of state, reconstruction, Riemann
  solver, implicit, sedimentation, the scalar module, the integrator) keep hand-written readers; their
  defaults live in their own files, and a key check there is that reader's, not the generator's.
- A deck is read once. Options built directly in code (a test, a Python script) skip the deck reader's checks,
  except the output domain checks, `OutputOptionsImpl::check_domain`
  ({{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl::check_domain >}}), which the block runs for every
  output however it was built.
- `distribute/backend` is accepted and ignored; the process-group backend comes from the `BACKEND` environment
  variable (the `backend` row of `layout.yaml`, {{< code src/options/layout.yaml >}}; @sec-appd).
- `conversion-order`, `x1-mass-covariance` and the stretched-grid keys have further setup checks in the hydro
  and coordinate modules (@sec-ch04 and @sec-ch03); the reader admits any integer or list, and the module refuses
  what it cannot run.
:::
